state.brief: The required appointment journey permits its addressed verified account or an authorized host manager to change times while keeping the prior room and host secured until success. The employee ledger and workspace ledger are independent storage authorities, separate again from local appointment records. Source-key reuse in the current employee reservation overwrites the earlier interval; choosing a distinct key instead causes overlapping old/new requests to conflict. The excerpt preserves real book/cancel admission and provider code. Only authored language/interface drafts are in scope: no implementation may be asserted and existing permissions must remain. Judge successful overlapping moves as well as failed reservations, delayed results and cancellation; reduction in code cannot justify dropping these behaviors.

reschedule_design.instructions: Choose the alternative most compatible with all documented movement constraints and costs.

criteria.staged: Extend both authoritative providers with provisional swaps. A candidate has a new source and an expected old source/revision; conflict checks omit only its own old allocation, both allocations remain protected while pending, and the appointment activates the candidates after both succeed before relinquishing old allocations. It meets overlap and recovery needs at the cost of explicit provider workflow bookkeeping.
criteria.disjoint: Use existing calls with new sources and reject any replacement interval intersecting the old reservations. The approach leaves the initial slot untouched on failure and needs less provider work, yet removes legitimate overlapping rescheduling.
criteria.coordinator: Consolidate room and employee ownership in a fresh atomic coordinator. One owner could settle the whole replacement together, but the required ownership migration introduces an architectural layer beyond current authority boundaries.

current_guarantee.instructions: Can independent use of the existing source-updating reserve/move interfaces alone ensure retention of the original slot whenever either side fails?

criteria.true: Old allocations remain secured for every separate-provider failure through the current source-level mechanisms as shown.
criteria.false: The actual mechanisms permit an old allocation to change before its counterpart succeeds, or do not substantiate complete preservation.
